{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the Java and Python SDKs as client libraries covering identity and signing, channel and chaincode operations, proposal creation, transaction submission, event handling, TLS configuration, and representative error handling.",
    "Use the existing Fabric wire protocols, cryptographic primitives, transaction formats, and peer/orderer APIs rather than introducing new protocols.",
    "Implement pre-built user chaincode through a peer-side external builder and launcher model with packaged chaincode metadata, rather than requiring peer-local source compilation.",
    "Provide pre-built chaincode support for the primary supported Linux container environments and document the packaging contract for additional environments.",
    "For certificate pinning, select the channel-loaded signed fingerprint-list approach. Fingerprint lists are signed by organization-controlled keys, configured in channel policy/configuration, validated deterministically by endorsers, and support key rollover.",
    "Expose VSCC validation diagnostics through structured validation errors so that peer logs and transaction failure events can include policy details, recognized signers, organizations, and missing policy requirements.",
    "Produce platform-specific release artifacts through the project build and CI/release process for the required command-line tools, including configtxgen, fabric-chaintool where applicable, and fabric-ca-client.",
    "Store complete documented default configuration files in a dedicated config_defaults directory and link them from the documentation and BYFN/test instructions.",
    "Use unit tests for component behavior, integration tests against a disposable multi-organization Fabric network, and regression tests for backward compatibility.",
    "Effort estimates include implementation, code review by the developer's self-review process, automated tests, integration testing, documentation, and local build/debug activities; they exclude elapsed waiting time for external reviews."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment is implemented against one selected, existing Fabric release line with stable peer, orderer, CA, and SDK APIs; migration across multiple major releases is out of scope.",
    "Existing Fabric cryptographic libraries, protobuf definitions, policy evaluation code, build tooling, and test-network infrastructure can be reused.",
    "The SDK requirements mean production-quality MVP client SDKs, not complete feature-for-feature parity with every existing or future Fabric SDK feature.",
    "The SDKs will initially target the primary supported Java and Python runtime versions and common Linux, macOS, and Windows development environments.",
    "The pre-built chaincode work includes peer integration, packaging metadata, launcher/build interfaces, validation, documentation, and representative chaincode examples, but not arbitrary third-party build systems.",
    "The pre-built chaincode implementation targets containerized deployment and the standard supported peer execution environments; specialized hardware, confidential execution, and nonstandard operating systems are excluded.",
    "Certificate fingerprint validation is performed during endorsement and uses channel configuration containing trusted roots, organization-controlled signing keys, and signed fingerprint lists; network-wide dynamic HTTP retrieval is excluded from the initial implementation.",
    "Certificate revocation protocols, OCSP, CRL distribution, and full CA implementation changes are excluded except where required to integrate fingerprint validation.",
    "VSCC diagnostics will identify available signer certificates and organizations and explain missing policy branches where the existing policy evaluator exposes sufficient information; redesigning the policy language is excluded.",
    "All required command-line tools already build from source in the repository, so release work focuses on reproducible packaging, cross-platform artifact generation, checksums, and documentation.",
    "The testing quick-start documentation will use the repository's existing test network and examples rather than creating a wholly new deployment framework.",
    "The complete default configuration set can be derived from existing configuration structs, defaults, templates, and documentation without changing unrelated runtime behavior.",
    "No dedicated additional developer, technical writer, release engineer, or QA engineer is assumed; the estimate represents one software developer performing all work."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and architecture design",
      "activity_description": "Refine the eight user stories into interfaces and acceptance criteria, inspect existing Fabric components, define SDK scope, pre-built chaincode packaging, certificate pinning configuration, diagnostic error structures, release artifacts, and configuration-file organization.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Java SDK implementation",
      "activity_description": "Implement the Java client library, including connection and TLS configuration, identities and signing, channel and chaincode APIs, proposal and transaction handling, event notifications, error mapping, examples, unit tests, and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 180
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Python SDK implementation",
      "activity_description": "Implement the Python client library with the corresponding core Fabric interaction capabilities, serialization and cryptographic integration, synchronous/asynchronous usage where appropriate, event handling, examples, unit tests, and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 180
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Pre-built user chaincode deployment",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement the external builder/launcher contract, chaincode package metadata and validation, peer integration, lifecycle/deployment handling, supported pre-built targets, failure reporting, example packages, compatibility tests, and operational documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 220
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "VSCC validation diagnostics and failure reporting",
      "activity_description": "Enhance policy validation failures with the evaluated policy, resolved signer identities and organizations, satisfied policy branches, and missing signer requirements; propagate structured details to logs and transaction/event failure interfaces; add policy regression and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 180
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Platform-specific tool binaries and release packaging",
      "activity_description": "Update build and CI/release scripts to produce downloadable binaries for configtxgen, fabric-chaintool where applicable, fabric-ca-client, and other required tools across supported platforms; add artifact naming, checksums, packaging validation, and user documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 120
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Certificate fingerprint-list validation",
      "activity_description": "Implement channel configuration for trusted roots, organization-controlled fingerprint-list signing keys, signed fingerprint-list parsing and verification, certificate fingerprint checking during endorsement, cache and key rollover handling, deterministic validation errors, configuration migration, and security-focused tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 320
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Testing quick-start network and documentation",
      "activity_description": "Organize existing test tools and readme files, add or repair quick-start scripts for starting a network and deploying test chaincode, document common tester workflows and extension points, and verify the instructions from a clean checkout.",
      "most_likely_effort": 100
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Complete default configuration set",
      "activity_description": "Inventory runtime defaults for peer, gossip, ledger, endorser, orderer, Kafka or equivalent ordering settings, and channel configuration; create complete config_defaults YAML files, validate generated values against code, update links and BYFN instructions, and add consistency checks.",
      "most_likely_effort": 120
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-component integration and regression testing",
      "activity_description": "Run end-to-end tests across peers, orderers, CA, SDKs, chaincode deployment, policy diagnostics, certificate validation, generated binaries, and default configurations; investigate failures, fix integration defects, and verify backward compatibility.",
      "most_likely_effort": 160
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Security, usability, and final quality pass",
      "activity_description": "Perform self-review of cryptographic and identity handling, policy information disclosure, input validation, packaging safety, API usability, logging behavior, documentation completeness, test coverage, and final cleanup of the increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 1700
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the Java and Python SDKs as client libraries covering identity and signing, channel and chaincode operations, proposal creation, transaction submission, event handling, TLS configuration, and representative error handling.
Use the existing Fabric wire protocols, cryptographic primitives, transaction formats, and peer/orderer APIs rather than introducing new protocols.
Implement pre-built user chaincode through a peer-side external builder and launcher model with packaged chaincode metadata, rather than requiring peer-local source compilation.
Provide pre-built chaincode support for the primary supported Linux container environments and document the packaging contract for additional environments.

For certificate pinning, select the channel-loaded signed fingerprint-list approach. Fingerprint lists are signed by organization-controlled keys, configured in channel policy/configuration, validated deterministically by endorsers, and support key rollover.

Expose VSCC validation diagnostics through structured validation errors so that peer logs and transaction failure events can include policy details, recognized signers, organizations, and missing policy requirements.

Produce platform-specific release artifacts through the project build and CI/release process for the required command-line tools, including configtxgen, fabric-chaintool where applicable, and fabric-ca-client.
Store complete documented default configuration files in a dedicated config_defaults directory and link them from the documentation and BYFN/test instructions.
Use unit tests for component behavior, integration tests against a disposable multi-organization Fabric network, and regression tests for backward compatibility.

Effort estimates include implementation, code review by the developer's self-review process, automated tests, integration testing, documentation, and local build/debug activities; they exclude elapsed waiting time for external reviews.
assumptions: The increment is implemented against one selected, existing Fabric release line with stable peer, orderer, CA, and SDK APIs; migration across multiple major releases is out of scope.
Existing Fabric cryptographic libraries, protobuf definitions, policy evaluation code, build tooling, and test-network infrastructure can be reused.
The SDK requirements mean production-quality MVP client SDKs, not complete feature-for-feature parity with every existing or future Fabric SDK feature.
The SDKs will initially target the primary supported Java and Python runtime versions and common Linux, macOS, and Windows development environments.

The pre-built chaincode work includes peer integration, packaging metadata, launcher/build interfaces, validation, documentation, and representative chaincode examples, but not arbitrary third-party build systems.

The pre-built chaincode implementation targets containerized deployment and the standard supported peer execution environments; specialized hardware, confidential execution, and nonstandard operating systems are excluded.

Certificate fingerprint validation is performed during endorsement and uses channel configuration containing trusted roots, organization-controlled signing keys, and signed fingerprint lists; network-wide dynamic HTTP retrieval is excluded from the initial implementation.
Certificate revocation protocols, OCSP, CRL distribution, and full CA implementation changes are excluded except where required to integrate fingerprint validation.

VSCC diagnostics will identify available signer certificates and organizations and explain missing policy branches where the existing policy evaluator exposes sufficient information; redesigning the policy language is excluded.
All required command-line tools already build from source in the repository, so release work focuses on reproducible packaging, cross-platform artifact generation, checksums, and documentation.
The testing quick-start documentation will use the repository's existing test network and examples rather than creating a wholly new deployment framework.
The complete default configuration set can be derived from existing configuration structs, defaults, templates, and documentation without changing unrelated runtime behavior.
No dedicated additional developer, technical writer, release engineer, or QA engineer is assumed; the estimate represents one software developer performing all work.

activities.activity_description: Refine the eight user stories into interfaces and acceptance criteria, inspect existing Fabric components, define SDK scope, pre-built chaincode packaging, certificate pinning configuration, diagnostic error structures, release artifacts, and configuration-file organization.

Implement the Java client library, including connection and TLS configuration, identities and signing, channel and chaincode APIs, proposal and transaction handling, event notifications, error mapping, examples, unit tests, and integration tests.

Implement the Python client library with the corresponding core Fabric interaction capabilities, serialization and cryptographic integration, synchronous/asynchronous usage where appropriate, event handling, examples, unit tests, and integration tests.

Design and implement the external builder/launcher contract, chaincode package metadata and validation, peer integration, lifecycle/deployment handling, supported pre-built targets, failure reporting, example packages, compatibility tests, and operational documentation.

activities.activity_description: Enhance policy validation failures with the evaluated policy, resolved signer identities and organizations, satisfied policy branches, and missing signer requirements; propagate structured details to logs and transaction/event failure interfaces; add policy regression and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Platform-specific tool binaries and release packaging
activities.activity_description: Update build and CI/release scripts to produce downloadable binaries for configtxgen, fabric-chaintool where applicable, fabric-ca-client, and other required tools across supported platforms; add artifact naming, checksums, packaging validation, and user documentation.

Implement channel configuration for trusted roots, organization-controlled fingerprint-list signing keys, signed fingerprint-list parsing and verification, certificate fingerprint checking during endorsement, cache and key rollover handling, deterministic validation errors, configuration migration, and security-focused tests.

Organize existing test tools and readme files, add or repair quick-start scripts for starting a network and deploying test chaincode, document common tester workflows and extension points, and verify the instructions from a clean checkout.

Inventory runtime defaults for peer, gossip, ledger, endorser, orderer, Kafka or equivalent ordering settings, and channel configuration; create complete config_defaults YAML files, validate generated values against code, update links and BYFN instructions, and add consistency checks.

Run end-to-end tests across peers, orderers, CA, SDKs, chaincode deployment, policy diagnostics, certificate validation, generated binaries, and default configurations; investigate failures, fix integration defects, and verify backward compatibility.
